title: Four People Just Finished a Year of Pretend Mars Life
summary: Four NASA volunteers have finally stepped outside after more than a year of living as if they were on Mars. The crew finished their pretend Mars trip on October 31, 2026. They never left Earth, but they lived like future Mars explorers. The four volunteers are Matthew Montgomery, James Spicer, Ross Elder, and Ellen Ellis. They were part of NASA's CHAPEA program, which studies how people handle long space trips. During the year, they did jobs that Mars explorers may need to do. They tested systems, grew crops, saved supplies, and did spacewalks — work outside their home. They also had to deal with slow messages from Earth. On Mars, radio signals take a long time to travel, so astronauts cannot get quick help from mission control. They must solve problems on their own. Keeping a crew healthy far from Earth is one of the hardest parts of going to Mars. NASA uses pretend missions like this to learn before real trips. What the crew learned will help NASA plan its Moon Base and future trips to Mars.
why_it_matters: One day astronauts may live on Mars, and pretend missions like this one teach us how people can stay healthy and work together far from home.
